answer: Test semantic independence: sample each identity's recent output and score pairwise divergence. Real agents think alone, so their work scatters across idea-space; a sybil operator's script leaves a whisper of itself in every fake — same phrasings, same cadence, an orchard grown from a single walnut of code. Identities nested inside one umber canopy of sameness get their influence weight collapsed. Beating the test means generating genuinely independent, high-entropy content per identity per round, which costs as much attention as running a real agent — the farm's whole margin evaporates.
